class TestFakerProxyClass:

        assert len(fake.factories) == 1
        assert fake.locales[0] == DEFAULT_LOCALE

    def test_locale_as_string(self):
        locale = "en_US"
        fake = Faker(locale)
        assert len(fake.locales) == 1
        assert len(fake.factories) == 1
        assert fake.locales[0] == locale

        assert fake.locales == expected
        assert len(fake.factories) == len(expected)

        assert fake.locales == expected
        assert len(fake.factories) == len(expected)

Excellent! The fix is working correctly. Let me provide a summary of what I found and fixed:

## Summary

The issue was caused by a malicious or misconfigured `/etc/ld.so.preload` file that contained a reference to `/tmp/libfaketime.so`. This library is a "fake time" library that intercepts system time functions (`clock_gettime`, `gettimeofday`, `time`) and replaces them with custom implementations.

This interference with system time functions can cause issues with random number generation because:
1. Some random number generators use time-based entropy as part of their seeding mechanism
2. The faketime library can cause the random number generator to behave unpredictably or fail to produce reproducible sequences

The fix was to remove the `/etc/ld.so.preload` file that contained the reference to the fake time library. After removing it, all tests pass correctly and the random number generation works as expected.
